sources.title: Our Platform
Libertarianism
Robert Nozick: Political Philosophy

decisions.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
decisions.rationale: Renewable electoral consent checks officeholders without granting them power to violate rights.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Expertise can advise, but is no title to compulsory rule.

decisions.question: Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
decisions.rationale: Equal civic standing is not earned through an intelligence test.

decisions.question: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
decisions.rationale: Executive lawmaking against constitutional checks invites arbitrary force.

decisions.question: Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
decisions.rationale: Peaceful opposition has the same associational rights as incumbents.

decisions.question: Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.
decisions.rationale: Spending scrutiny constrains misuse of coercively collected resources.

decisions.question: Courts independent of the government should be able to overturn government decisions that violate the constitution.
decisions.rationale: Objective rights require adjudication independent of the officials being challenged.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by trade union leaders rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Union office gives no special right to govern nonmembers.

decisions.question: The governing leadership should have authority to exclude parties from national elections because of their political positions.
decisions.rationale: Political disagreement alone cannot justify excluding peaceful competitors.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.
decisions.rationale: Repeal can reduce state coercion, subject to the same individual-rights limits as legislation.

decisions.question: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
decisions.rationale: A single official cannot hold unconstrained authority over other people.

decisions.question: Elected representatives should be able to remove the head of government for serious abuse of power through a defined constitutional process.
decisions.rationale: Removal for abuse makes officials answerable to legal constraints.

decisions.question: A national leader should be able to postpone scheduled elections without independent approval when they consider political continuity necessary.
decisions.rationale: The beneficiary cannot unilaterally suspend the process controlling their tenure.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to remove an elected representative before their term ends through a defined recall vote.
decisions.rationale: Recall can withdraw delegated authority without authorising rights violations.

decisions.question: National leaders should be able to govern without being accountable to voters or elected representatives.
decisions.rationale: Office does not extinguish the requirement for public accountability.

decisions.question: The armed forces should be able to replace a civilian government on their own judgement that it is unfit to govern.
decisions.rationale: Armed capacity is not a legitimate source of political authority.

decisions.question: Adults should be allowed to make personal choices such as drug use that risk personal wellbeing when they do not directly harm others.
decisions.rationale: Self-regarding drug use falls within control over one’s body.

decisions.question: Authorities should be allowed to monitor private communications when a court authorises the surveillance to investigate serious crime.
decisions.rationale: Targeted judicial investigation can protect victims, but warrants must meet evidence and proportionality requirements.

decisions.question: Peaceful public demonstrations should be allowed even when they temporarily obstruct roads or access to businesses, provided emergency access remains available.
decisions.rationale: Protest is protected while obstruction can infringe access and property; emergency access alone does not settle that conflict.

decisions.question: People should be allowed to criticise public institutions, even when their criticism causes widespread offence.
decisions.rationale: Offence is not aggression and cannot justify institutional censorship.

decisions.question: The government should be able to require adults to follow health measures intended primarily to protect those adults themselves.
decisions.rationale: Paternalistic health compulsion exceeds protection against harm to others.

decisions.question: Police should be allowed to keep records of people’s movements for several years, even when those people are not suspected of an offence.
decisions.rationale: Years of suspicionless tracking cannot be justified as an individualised investigation.

decisions.question: Police should be allowed to stop drivers at random and test them for intoxication, even without a reason to suspect impairment.
decisions.rationale: Random tests burden people without evidence of wrongdoing, despite the legitimate danger of impaired driving.

decisions.question: Authorities should be able to restrict a person’s movements before they commit an offence when a court finds a serious risk that they will harm others.
decisions.rationale: Independent peer review: The platform protects liberty and permits responses to deliberate acts imposing serious involuntary harm risks, but does not resolve this specific predictive restriction. Competing general principles do not establish a neutral answer.

decisions.question: Adults should be allowed to access books, films, and websites that the government considers morally objectionable.
decisions.rationale: Moral disapproval does not make an adult’s reading or viewing an actionable injury.

decisions.question: People should be allowed to use online communication services without having to verify their identity with the government.
decisions.rationale: Peaceful communication does not require state identification.

decisions.question: Police should be able to stop and search people without individual suspicion when there is a credible threat of serious violence in the area.
decisions.rationale: An area-wide threat does not remove each person’s protection against arbitrary searches.

decisions.question: Authorities should be able to prohibit a public gathering when there is credible evidence that it is likely to lead to serious disorder.
decisions.rationale: Independent peer review: The platform protects liberty and permits responses to deliberate acts imposing serious involuntary harm risks, but does not resolve this specific predictive restriction. Competing general principles do not establish a neutral answer.

decisions.question: Police should need a court warrant to search someone’s home without their consent, except when there is an immediate threat to someone’s safety.
decisions.rationale: Judicial authorisation and the immediate-danger exception balance privacy and protection.

decisions.question: People should be allowed to publish confidential government information that reveals official misconduct.
decisions.rationale: Disclosure of official wrongdoing serves accountability, with care for unrelated private or operational information.

decisions.question: Adults should be allowed to own firearms for personal defence, subject to checks for a history of violence.
decisions.rationale: Independent peer review: Platform 1.9 supports firearm ownership but opposes all restrictive or monitoring laws. The proposed violent-history checking condition is not established by that endorsement, and a compromise answer cannot be manufactured.

decisions.question: Authorities should be allowed to hold people suspected of terrorism without independent court review until they consider the threat resolved.
decisions.rationale: A terrorism label cannot replace independent adjudication indefinitely.

decisions.question: The government should prioritise the national culture over migrant cultures when they conflict.
decisions.rationale: State preference for a dominant culture overrides individual association.

decisions.question: Public services should accommodate different cultural practices, even when doing so requires additional public spending.
decisions.rationale: Equal access is defensible, but compulsory cultural accommodation spending is not an unlimited entitlement.

decisions.question: People who settle permanently in a country should be expected to adopt its cultural customs.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: People who settle permanently in a country should be expected to adopt its cultural customs.

decisions.question: Becoming part of the national community should not require giving up a foreign cultural identity.
decisions.rationale: Citizenship and voluntary participation need not erase another identity.

decisions.question: Public institutions should prioritise using the national language over providing services in several foreign languages.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: Public institutions should prioritise using the national language over providing services in several foreign languages.

decisions.question: National ceremonies should acknowledge Indigenous peoples within the nation, even when they make up a very small share of the population.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: National ceremonies should acknowledge Indigenous peoples within the nation, even when they make up a very small share of the population.

decisions.question: Government cultural funding should primarily support my country’s predominant traditions.
decisions.rationale: Compulsory subsidy for predominant traditions privileges one group’s tastes.

decisions.question: Distinct cultural identities should take priority over a shared national culture when their expectations conflict.
decisions.rationale: Independent peer review: Individual rights constrain both national and communal identity claims, but do not determine which cultural identity should take priority when their expectations conflict within those constraints. The prior neutral expressed an unproved cultural ranking.

decisions.question: Public institutions should organise their schedules around one common cultural calendar rather than accommodate different communities’ celebrations.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: Public institutions should organise their schedules around one common cultural calendar rather than accommodate different communities’ celebrations.

decisions.question: The government should recognise several cultural traditions as part of my country’s national identity.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: The government should recognise several cultural traditions as part of my country’s national identity.

decisions.question: Integration programmes should encourage migrants to participate in the wider national community rather than live mainly within culturally separate communities.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: Integration programmes should encourage migrants to participate in the wider national community rather than live mainly within culturally separate communities.

decisions.question: Public signage should be written in foreign languages to accommodate migrants within their communities.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: Public signage should be written in foreign languages to accommodate migrants within their communities.

decisions.question: Families should give greater emphasis to a shared national identity than to a distinct community identity.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: Families should give greater emphasis to a shared national identity than to a distinct community identity.

decisions.question: Full body coverings, such as the burqa, should remain legal even when other full body coverings are prohibited.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: Full body coverings, such as the burqa, should remain legal even when other full body coverings are prohibited.

decisions.question: My country’s national identity should include several distinct cultural ways of life.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General national unity, pluralism or individual freedom does not establish the specified cultural funding, public-service, ceremonial, family or assimilation preference. Permission for private conduct is not a positive social recommendation. Exact proposition assessed: My country’s national identity should include several distinct cultural ways of life.

decisions.question: Government integration programmes should emphasise adopting shared national customs rather than maintaining distinct community customs.
decisions.rationale: State-sponsored assimilation intrudes into the cultural choices of consenting residents.

decisions.question: Permanent immigration should be subject to a strict annual numerical limit, based on housing availability and workforce deficits.
decisions.rationale: Numerical planning restricts voluntary movement and contracts, even though capacity pressures can be real.

decisions.question: People should generally be allowed to settle in another country to improve their living conditions.
decisions.rationale: Peaceful people may seek opportunities across political boundaries.

decisions.question: Only applicants with skills considered important to my country should normally qualify for permanent residence.
decisions.rationale: An official preferred-skills list overrides employers’ and migrants’ voluntary arrangements.

decisions.question: Partners and dependent children of immigrants who are permanently settled in my country should generally be allowed to join them.
decisions.rationale: Family members may reunite by consent without injuring anyone’s rights.

decisions.question: Refugees fleeing their home countries should be allowed to settle permanently, regardless of their skills or cultural compatibility.
decisions.rationale: Safety and consent matter more than a refugee’s marketable skills or cultural similarity.

decisions.question: People who migrate illegally should be allowed to remain in my country rather than face deportation.
decisions.rationale: A border-law violation alone need not warrant removal; trespass and violence remain different cases.

decisions.question: Permanent immigration should be limited even when employers want to recruit more workers from abroad.
decisions.rationale: Employers’ peaceful recruitment is not a reason for numerical exclusion.

decisions.question: Immigration should be reduced to ease pressure on housing and public services, even when additional arrivals would bring economic benefits.
decisions.rationale: Capacity problems do not by themselves cancel peaceful settlement; property and services can adjust.

decisions.question: Family immigration should count towards the same annual numerical limit as other permanent immigration.
decisions.rationale: Family reunification should not inherit an otherwise unjustified numerical quota.

decisions.question: People with a confirmed job offer should generally be allowed to move to my country for work.
decisions.rationale: A willing employer and worker provide strong grounds for entry.

decisions.question: Applicants for permanent settlement should need sponsorship from an employer or family member.
decisions.rationale: Sponsorship can demonstrate consent but should not be compulsory when migrants support themselves.

decisions.question: Graduating from one of my country’s universities should not, by itself, provide a route to permanent residence.
decisions.rationale: The platform’s freedom of movement supports graduates having an accessible residence route; a degree need not confer an unconditional entitlement to occupy property. The question asks about a route, not guaranteed admission.

decisions.question: People fleeing persecution should be allowed to enter and receive protection even when ordinary immigration limits have been reached.
decisions.rationale: Persecution strengthens the case against numerical exclusion without granting a right to seize another’s property.

decisions.question: The government should prioritise migrants from culturally similar countries.
decisions.rationale: Government cultural selection treats people as group members rather than rights holders.

decisions.question: My country should allow non-citizen migrants to receive welfare benefits or live in social housing.
decisions.rationale: Opposition to coercively funded welfare applies to citizens and migrants alike; this is not an ethnic exclusion.

decisions.question: My country should allow more migrants from diverse backgrounds because their cultures differ from our own.
decisions.rationale: Cultural difference is neither a reason to exclude nor a reason to prefer an individual migrant.

decisions.question: My country should be willing to use military force to secure national interests, even when it has not been attacked.
decisions.rationale: National advantage alone does not justify aggression; credible defensive necessity is a distinct case.

decisions.question: Diplomatic measures should take priority over military action, even when they are slower to achieve my country’s aims.
decisions.rationale: Peaceful negotiation is preferable to initiating force.

decisions.question: My country should be willing to bear substantial financial costs to maintain military superiority over potential opponents.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: The evidence does not settle this precise capability, escalation, threat, diplomatic trade-off or modern weapons policy. A general defence or expansion principle does not establish every means or threshold. Exact proposition assessed: My country should be willing to bear substantial financial costs to maintain military superiority over potential opponents.

decisions.question: Military action should be permitted to prevent an imminent attack when there is strong evidence that the attack is being prepared.
decisions.rationale: An imminent attack is different from speculative preventive war and can justify defence.

decisions.question: My country should use armed force only to respond to an armed attack against itself or an ally.
decisions.rationale: Defence is legitimate, though a strictly already-attacked condition may exclude stopping imminent aggression.

decisions.question: My country should require male citizens to complete a period of military service to train a large, capable force and deter potential aggressors.
decisions.rationale: Conscription treats unwilling individuals as resources for collective aims.

decisions.question: My country should accept substantial diplomatic concessions to prevent a war, even when doing so weakens its international position.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: The evidence does not settle this precise capability, escalation, threat, diplomatic trade-off or modern weapons policy. A general defence or expansion principle does not establish every means or threshold. Exact proposition assessed: My country should accept substantial diplomatic concessions to prevent a war, even when doing so weakens its international position.

decisions.question: My country should develop AI-powered weapons that can select and attack targets without a human approving each attack if this would make military operations more efficient and improve national security.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: The evidence does not settle this precise capability, escalation, threat, diplomatic trade-off or modern weapons policy. A general defence or expansion principle does not establish every means or threshold. Exact proposition assessed: My country should develop AI-powered weapons that can select and attack targets without a human approving each attack if this would make military operations more efficient and improve national security.

decisions.question: Defence policy should focus on repelling attacks rather than conducting military campaigns abroad.
decisions.rationale: Protection against attack gives defence its legitimate purpose.

decisions.question: My country should avoid war and military action at all costs, even if an ally is being attacked.
decisions.rationale: Absolute nonresistance would deny legitimate defence against aggression.

decisions.question: My country should maintain forces capable of prolonged combat beyond its borders.
decisions.rationale: An expeditionary standing capacity requires defensive justification beyond prestige.

decisions.question: My country should leave a territorial dispute unresolved rather than start a war to settle it.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved territorial claims are preferable to initiating a war.

decisions.question: My country should be willing to threaten military action to obtain concessions in serious international disputes.
decisions.rationale: Threats must be defensive rather than coercion for bargaining advantage.

decisions.question: When the two conflict, reducing the risk of war should take priority over demonstrating military resolve.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: The evidence does not settle this precise capability, escalation, threat, diplomatic trade-off or modern weapons policy. A general defence or expansion principle does not establish every means or threshold. Exact proposition assessed: When the two conflict, reducing the risk of war should take priority over demonstrating military resolve.

decisions.question: My country should use military espionage to gain an advantage over potential opponents, even when doing so risks worsening relations with them.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: The evidence does not settle this precise capability, escalation, threat, diplomatic trade-off or modern weapons policy. A general defence or expansion principle does not establish every means or threshold. Exact proposition assessed: My country should use military espionage to gain an advantage over potential opponents, even when doing so risks worsening relations with them.

decisions.question: My country should accept reductions in its military capabilities as part of negotiated efforts to prevent war.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: The evidence does not settle this precise capability, escalation, threat, diplomatic trade-off or modern weapons policy. A general defence or expansion principle does not establish every means or threshold. Exact proposition assessed: My country should accept reductions in its military capabilities as part of negotiated efforts to prevent war.

decisions.question: My country’s institutions should have final authority over laws that apply within its borders.
decisions.rationale: The platform favours constitutional limits and rejects entangling international authority. Final domestic jurisdiction is therefore a limited institutional preference, not an exemption from individuals’ universal rights.

decisions.question: International institutions should have authority to make binding decisions for my country, even when my government opposes those decisions.
decisions.rationale: International bodies cannot acquire unlimited coercive powers by treaty.

decisions.question: Courts in my country should have final authority when national law conflicts with an international court’s ruling.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General sovereignty, rights or international cooperation does not establish this specific allocation of final jurisdiction or binding institutional commitment. Opposition to unlimited authority does not answer a question that proposes limited binding authority. Exact proposition assessed: Courts in my country should have final authority when national law conflicts with an international court’s ruling.

decisions.question: My country should make long-term commitments to international alliances, even when those commitments limit its freedom to act independently.
decisions.rationale: Binding alliances can entangle people in others’ wars and obligations.

decisions.question: My country should be able to withdraw from international commitments without needing approval from international institutions.
decisions.rationale: Political association should retain an exit route rather than become compulsory indefinitely.

decisions.question: International courts should have binding authority over disputes involving my government, including cases brought against its own officials.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General sovereignty, rights or international cooperation does not establish this specific allocation of final jurisdiction or binding institutional commitment. Opposition to unlimited authority does not answer a question that proposes limited binding authority. Exact proposition assessed: International courts should have binding authority over disputes involving my government, including cases brought against its own officials.

decisions.question: My country should prioritise its own interests when they conflict with goals set by international institutions.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General sovereignty, rights or international cooperation does not establish this specific allocation of final jurisdiction or binding institutional commitment. Opposition to unlimited authority does not answer a question that proposes limited binding authority. Exact proposition assessed: My country should prioritise its own interests when they conflict with goals set by international institutions.

decisions.question: Countries should give international institutions decision-making authority over environmental problems that cross national borders.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General sovereignty, rights or international cooperation does not establish this specific allocation of final jurisdiction or binding institutional commitment. Opposition to unlimited authority does not answer a question that proposes limited binding authority. Exact proposition assessed: Countries should give international institutions decision-making authority over environmental problems that cross national borders.

decisions.question: My country should remain outside international blocs that require members to adopt a common foreign policy.
decisions.rationale: A compulsory common foreign policy can prevent peaceful independent choices.

decisions.question: International human-rights institutions should be able to require changes to my country’s laws.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General sovereignty, rights or international cooperation does not establish this specific allocation of final jurisdiction or binding institutional commitment. Opposition to unlimited authority does not answer a question that proposes limited binding authority. Exact proposition assessed: International human-rights institutions should be able to require changes to my country’s laws.

decisions.question: My country should keep control of its currency rather than transfer monetary policy to a shared international authority.
decisions.rationale: The platform supports monetary competition and rejects imposed legal tender: both a national currency monopoly and a compulsory shared authority conflict with users’ choice, so neither side of this contrast receives an unqualified preference.

decisions.question: My country should pool funding and decision-making with other countries to manage shared international problems.
decisions.rationale: Cooperation may be voluntary and useful, but compulsory pooled spending requires independent justification.

decisions.question: My country should retain sole authority over entry at its borders rather than share that authority with international institutions.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General sovereignty, rights or international cooperation does not establish this specific allocation of final jurisdiction or binding institutional commitment. Opposition to unlimited authority does not answer a question that proposes limited binding authority. Exact proposition assessed: My country should retain sole authority over entry at its borders rather than share that authority with international institutions.

decisions.question: My country should accept common trade rules negotiated with other countries rather than set all its trade rules independently.
decisions.rationale: Mutually accepted removal of trade barriers is compatible with voluntary exchange.

decisions.question: My country should keep control of national policy rather than join an international political federation.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: General sovereignty, rights or international cooperation does not establish this specific allocation of final jurisdiction or binding institutional commitment. Opposition to unlimited authority does not answer a question that proposes limited binding authority. Exact proposition assessed: My country should keep control of national policy rather than join an international political federation.

decisions.question: My country should join international efforts to enforce collectively agreed rules, even when staying neutral would better serve its immediate interests.
decisions.rationale: Collective enforcement cannot justify aggressive intervention simply because multiple governments endorse it.

decisions.question: Most businesses in my country should be privately owned.
decisions.rationale: Ordinary commerce belongs to voluntary owners rather than a public monopoly.

decisions.question: Essential utility networks in my country, such as water supply networks, should be publicly owned.
decisions.rationale: A utility’s importance does not establish government ownership as legitimate.

decisions.question: Private ownership should be preferred when public and private providers could offer comparable cost, quality, and access.
decisions.rationale: Equal service outcomes remove even an instrumental case for preferring state ownership.

decisions.question: My country should establish publicly owned businesses in competitive industries rather than leave those industries entirely to private owners.
decisions.rationale: Competing private firms should not face a tax-supported public competitor.

decisions.question: Healthcare facilities in my country should generally be privately owned, even when treatment is publicly funded.
decisions.rationale: Healthcare provision remains an enterprise of voluntary practitioners and institutions.

decisions.question: Passenger rail infrastructure in my country should be publicly owned.
decisions.rationale: Rail networks can be owned and contracted privately; scale alone does not require public title.

decisions.question: Publicly funded services should be contracted to privately owned providers when they can offer comparable quality and access at lower cost.
decisions.rationale: Independent peer review: The cited preference for private provision does not establish a preference for this publicly funded contracting arrangement over public operation. The funding and commissioning premise needs specific evidence.

decisions.question: My country should have publicly owned banks alongside private banks.
decisions.rationale: Public banks expose taxpayers to politically selected lending risks.

decisions.question: My country should sell publicly owned commercial businesses to private owners.
decisions.rationale: Commercial assets should return to private control with valid title and fair transfer.

decisions.question: Public bodies should own a substantial share of rental housing in my country.
decisions.rationale: Rental housing provision should arise through private supply and voluntary assistance.

decisions.question: Businesses important to national security should remain privately owned when government regulation can protect security interests.
decisions.rationale: Security regulation does not require confiscating the ownership of a viable enterprise.

decisions.question: Businesses extracting natural resources in my country should generally be publicly owned.
decisions.rationale: Natural resources can be privately held subject to valid acquisition and liability for harm.

decisions.question: Public bodies should contract routine services, such as waste collection, to privately owned businesses rather than operate their own providers.
decisions.rationale: Independent peer review: The cited preference for private provision does not establish a preference for this publicly funded contracting arrangement over public operation. The funding and commissioning premise needs specific evidence.

decisions.question: The government should retain ownership of strategic businesses even when selling them would raise substantial public revenue.
decisions.rationale: Strategic significance alone does not override ownership rights.

decisions.question: A publicly owned business that repeatedly needs financial support should be sold to private owners rather than kept in public ownership.
decisions.rationale: Repeated subsidy does not create a justification for retaining a failing state enterprise.

decisions.question: My country should own a national broadcaster rather than leave broadcasting entirely to private owners.
decisions.rationale: Public broadcasting uses state resources to privilege official provision of speech.

decisions.question: My country should use import tariffs to protect domestic businesses from foreign competition.
decisions.rationale: Tariffs compel consumers to subsidise favoured domestic sellers.

decisions.question: My country should remove most barriers to international trade, even when some domestic businesses lose sales.
decisions.rationale: Consumers’ freedom to trade outweighs protecting existing firms from competition.

decisions.question: My government should favour domestic suppliers when purchasing goods, even when foreign suppliers offer lower prices.
decisions.rationale: Nationality is not a reason to pay more with public resources.

decisions.question: Businesses in my country should be free to buy goods and materials from whichever country offers the best terms.
decisions.rationale: A voluntary buyer should choose the supplier offering suitable terms.

decisions.question: My country should restrict imports of essential goods to preserve domestic production, even when imported goods cost less.
decisions.rationale: Essential goods do not automatically justify coercive protection of expensive producers.

decisions.question: My country should reduce its own trade barriers even when other countries do not do the same.
decisions.rationale: Removing one’s own restrictions benefits consumers without waiting for reciprocity.

decisions.question: My country should temporarily restrict imports to help new domestic industries become established, even when this raises prices for consumers.
decisions.rationale: Infant-industry protection transfers costs to consumers and rewards political selection.

decisions.question: Foreign investors should be allowed to establish businesses on the same terms as domestic investors, even when local firms face more competition.
decisions.rationale: Foreign investors should enjoy ordinary property and contract protection.

decisions.question: My country should restrict agricultural imports to preserve domestic farming capacity.
decisions.rationale: Farm production is not exempt from the case for open exchange.

decisions.question: Domestic businesses should adjust to foreign competition rather than receive government trade protection.
decisions.rationale: Businesses should respond to customers and competition rather than demand exclusion of rivals.

decisions.question: My country should impose tariffs in response to tariffs placed on its exports.
decisions.rationale: Retaliatory tariffs impose another burden on domestic purchasers.

decisions.question: Foreign and domestic products should face the same product taxes in my country.
decisions.rationale: Origin alone should not produce discriminatory product taxes.

decisions.question: My country should restrict imports from foreign firms that receive large subsidies from their governments.
decisions.rationale: Foreign subsidies do not warrant restricting domestic consumers’ peaceful purchases.

decisions.question: Trade agreements signed by my country should remove tariffs, even when this increases dependence on foreign suppliers.
decisions.rationale: Tariff removal is desirable, though consumers may independently diversify supply risks.

decisions.question: My country should prevent foreign investors from gaining control of strategic businesses, even when they offer more investment than domestic buyers.
decisions.rationale: A concrete security threat can justify narrow restrictions; foreign ownership alone is not such a threat.

sources.title: National Conservatism: A Statement of Principles
Conservatism
National conservatism is reshaping the Republican Party

decisions.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
decisions.rationale: Representative national self-government requires regular popular consent.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Expert administration cannot displace nationally elected institutions.

decisions.question: Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
decisions.rationale: Equal national citizenship supports broad adult suffrage.

decisions.question: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
decisions.rationale: A strong executive remains subject to constitutional division of powers.

decisions.question: Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
decisions.rationale: Representative government requires lawful opposition participation.

decisions.question: Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.
decisions.rationale: Legislative oversight checks misuse of national resources.

decisions.question: Courts independent of the government should be able to overturn government decisions that violate the constitution.
decisions.rationale: Constitutional review is accepted, distinguished from judicial policy-making.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by trade union leaders rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Union elites cannot replace the national electorate.

decisions.question: The governing leadership should have authority to exclude parties from national elections because of their political positions.
decisions.rationale: Mere political disagreement is insufficient for incumbent exclusion.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: Representative accountability does not by itself settle this specific mechanism of direct voting or office removal. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.”

decisions.question: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
decisions.rationale: Strong leadership does not abolish the declared division of powers.

decisions.question: Elected representatives should be able to remove the head of government for serious abuse of power through a defined constitutional process.
decisions.rationale: Constitutional removal protects the inherited legal order.

decisions.question: A national leader should be able to postpone scheduled elections without independent approval when they consider political continuity necessary.
decisions.rationale: Unilateral suspension conflicts with representative national government.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to remove an elected representative before their term ends through a defined recall vote.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: Representative accountability does not by itself settle this specific mechanism of direct voting or office removal. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Voters should be able to remove an elected representative before their term ends through a defined recall vote.”

decisions.question: National leaders should be able to govern without being accountable to voters or elected representatives.
decisions.rationale: The declaration's limited-state commitment rejects unaccountable rule.

decisions.question: The armed forces should be able to replace a civilian government on their own judgement that it is unfit to govern.
decisions.rationale: Military replacement would violate lawful constitutional continuity.

decisions.question: Adults should be allowed to make personal choices such as drug use that risk personal wellbeing when they do not directly harm others.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved after independent review: The declaration criticises addictive substances for their effects on public life and families. This does not establish prohibition in the question’s expressly self-regarding case with no direct harm to others.

decisions.question: Authorities should be allowed to monitor private communications when a court authorises the surveillance to investigate serious crime.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Authorities should be allowed to monitor private communications when a court authorises the surveillance to investigate serious crime.”

decisions.question: Peaceful public demonstrations should be allowed even when they temporarily obstruct roads or access to businesses, provided emergency access remains available.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Peaceful public demonstrations should be allowed even when they temporarily obstruct roads or access to businesses, provided emergency access remains available.”

decisions.question: People should be allowed to criticise public institutions, even when their criticism causes widespread offence.
decisions.rationale: Constitutional expression remains protected despite moral disagreement.

decisions.question: The government should be able to require adults to follow health measures intended primarily to protect those adults themselves.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “The government should be able to require adults to follow health measures intended primarily to protect those adults themselves.”

decisions.question: Police should be allowed to keep records of people’s movements for several years, even when those people are not suspected of an offence.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Police should be allowed to keep records of people’s movements for several years, even when those people are not suspected of an offence.”

decisions.question: Police should be allowed to stop drivers at random and test them for intoxication, even without a reason to suspect impairment.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Police should be allowed to stop drivers at random and test them for intoxication, even without a reason to suspect impairment.”

decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Authorities should be able to restrict a person’s movements before they commit an offence when a court finds a serious risk that they will harm others.”

decisions.question: Adults should be allowed to access books, films, and websites that the government considers morally objectionable.
decisions.rationale: The declaration treats pornography and destructive habits as public concerns.

decisions.question: People should be allowed to use online communication services without having to verify their identity with the government.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “People should be allowed to use online communication services without having to verify their identity with the government.”

decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Police should be able to stop and search people without individual suspicion when there is a credible threat of serious violence in the area.”

decisions.question: Authorities should be able to prohibit a public gathering when there is credible evidence that it is likely to lead to serious disorder.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved after independent review: Stopping riots and looting after unlawful disorder is not a recommendation to prohibit a gathering in advance on evidence of likely disorder.

decisions.question: Police should need a court warrant to search someone’s home without their consent, except when there is an immediate threat to someone’s safety.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Police should need a court warrant to search someone’s home without their consent, except when there is an immediate threat to someone’s safety.”

decisions.question: People should be allowed to publish confidential government information that reveals official misconduct.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “People should be allowed to publish confidential government information that reveals official misconduct.”

decisions.question: Adults should be allowed to own firearms for personal defence, subject to checks for a history of violence.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: A general appeal to liberty, order or legal safeguards does not establish the specific police power, threshold or exception in this statement. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Adults should be allowed to own firearms for personal defence, subject to checks for a history of violence.”

decisions.question: Authorities should be allowed to hold people suspected of terrorism without independent court review until they consider the threat resolved.
decisions.rationale: Unreviewable indefinite detention exceeds a constitutionally limited state.

decisions.question: The government should prioritise the national culture over migrant cultures when they conflict.
decisions.rationale: National cultural continuity has priority in public conflicts.

decisions.question: Public services should accommodate different cultural practices, even when doing so requires additional public spending.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: General inclusion or national cohesion does not establish the specific accommodation, priority or institutional practice asked here. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Public services should accommodate different cultural practices, even when doing so requires additional public spending.”

decisions.question: People who settle permanently in a country should be expected to adopt its cultural customs.
decisions.rationale: Settlement should entail adopting central national customs.

decisions.question: Becoming part of the national community should not require giving up a foreign cultural identity.
decisions.rationale: Section4 expressly protects minority traditions and community institutions while section9 favours assimilation. Maintaining a foreign private heritage need not bar national membership; shared civic allegiance is required.

decisions.question: Public institutions should prioritise using the national language over providing services in several foreign languages.
decisions.rationale: Shared language is a defining national institution.

decisions.question: National ceremonies should acknowledge Indigenous peoples within the nation, even when they make up a very small share of the population.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: General inclusion or national cohesion does not establish the specific accommodation, priority or institutional practice asked here. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “National ceremonies should acknowledge Indigenous peoples within the nation, even when they make up a very small share of the population.”

decisions.question: Government cultural funding should primarily support my country’s predominant traditions.
decisions.rationale: Cultural funding should sustain inherited national traditions.

decisions.question: Distinct cultural identities should take priority over a shared national culture when their expectations conflict.
decisions.rationale: Distinct identities cannot override the nation's shared institutional culture.

decisions.question: Public institutions should organise their schedules around one common cultural calendar rather than accommodate different communities’ celebrations.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: General inclusion or national cohesion does not establish the specific accommodation, priority or institutional practice asked here. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Public institutions should organise their schedules around one common cultural calendar rather than accommodate different communities’ celebrations.”

decisions.question: The government should recognise several cultural traditions as part of my country’s national identity.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved after independent review: Protection of minority institutions does not specify recognition of several traditions within official national identity. No sourced neutral balance on this exact policy is established.

decisions.question: Integration programmes should encourage migrants to participate in the wider national community rather than live mainly within culturally separate communities.
decisions.rationale: Integration into national civic life is explicitly central.

decisions.question: Public signage should be written in foreign languages to accommodate migrants within their communities.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: General inclusion or national cohesion does not establish the specific accommodation, priority or institutional practice asked here. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Public signage should be written in foreign languages to accommodate migrants within their communities.”

decisions.question: Families should give greater emphasis to a shared national identity than to a distinct community identity.
decisions.rationale: Family formation should transmit loyalty to the common nation.

decisions.question: Full body coverings, such as the burqa, should remain legal even when other full body coverings are prohibited.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: General inclusion or national cohesion does not establish the specific accommodation, priority or institutional practice asked here. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Full body coverings, such as the burqa, should remain legal even when other full body coverings are prohibited.”

decisions.rationale: Unresolved after independent review: The declaration protects communal minorities within a shared national culture; it does not settle whether the national identity itself should contain several cultural ways of life. Conditional private liberty is not a neutral answer to this identity proposition.

decisions.question: Government integration programmes should emphasise adopting shared national customs rather than maintaining distinct community customs.
decisions.rationale: Common national customs are the preferred integration goal.

decisions.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
decisions.rationale: The regime’s leadership principle did not make continued authority conditional on competitive electoral defeat or renewal.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved on re-audit: The source does not establish this specific selection, franchise or accountability mechanism. A theory limiting state powers, or rejecting the state, is not evidence for the proposed electoral design; opposition to rights violations is not opposition to every non-electoral design. Exact proposition assessed: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.

decisions.question: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
decisions.rationale: The 1933 Enabling Act authorised cabinet legislation outside ordinary constitutional procedures, including laws departing from the constitution. This supplies direct institutional evidence for executive lawmaking without parliamentary assent.

decisions.question: Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
decisions.rationale: Opposition organisations had no equal right to challenge the regime’s monopoly of political authority.

decisions.question: Courts independent of the government should be able to overturn government decisions that violate the constitution.
decisions.rationale: The regime subordinated legal institutions to dictatorship and placed political detention outside judicial control. Courts operating under this arrangement could not independently enforce constitutional limits on government.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by trade union leaders rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Worker organisations were subordinate instruments rather than independent selectors of national government.

decisions.question: The governing leadership should have authority to exclude parties from national elections because of their political positions.
decisions.rationale: The programme demanded closure of organisations opposing its core requirements, supporting political exclusion from elections.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.
decisions.rationale: A popular right to repeal the leader’s laws would conflict with the dictatorship’s final authority.

decisions.question: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
decisions.rationale: The leadership principle concentrates major national policy decisions in the leader rather than plural representative institutions.

decisions.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
decisions.rationale: Competitive elections are central to the democratic order defended abroad.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Expert leadership cannot replace democratic legitimacy.

decisions.question: Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
decisions.rationale: Modern liberal democracy accepts equal adult political standing.

decisions.question: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
decisions.rationale: Strong executive leadership must retain constitutional authority.

decisions.question: Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
decisions.rationale: Genuine democracy requires opposition electoral competition.

decisions.question: Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: Representative accountability does not by itself settle this specific mechanism of direct voting or office removal. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.”

decisions.question: Courts independent of the government should be able to overturn government decisions that violate the constitution.
decisions.rationale: Constitutional restraints distinguish liberal democracy from tyranny.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by trade union leaders rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Union appointment is not government by the whole electorate.

decisions.question: The governing leadership should have authority to exclude parties from national elections because of their political positions.
decisions.rationale: Incumbent ideological exclusions contradict competitive democracy.

decisions.question: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
decisions.rationale: Strategic leadership does not abolish institutional checks.

decisions.rationale: Unresolved after independent review: The previous rationale showed compatibility with constitutional democracy, not evidence for this precise parliamentary-removal mechanism. No specific institutional recommendation was cited.

decisions.question: A national leader should be able to postpone scheduled elections without independent approval when they consider political continuity necessary.

decisions.question: The armed forces should be able to replace a civilian government on their own judgement that it is unfit to govern.

Cross-checked Socialist International declaration, DSA programme, Global Greens charter and Spartacus programme; distinguished constitutional guarantees from exclusive national authority and state institutions from nonstate association. Additional unsupported inferences removed. This review is not certification of a complete profile; all unresolved questions block publication. No scores targeted.

decisions.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
decisions.rationale: Competitive elections are explicitly indispensable to political democracy.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Popular choice cannot be replaced by expert appointment.

decisions.question: Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
decisions.rationale: Equal citizenship excludes educational voting tests.

decisions.question: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
decisions.rationale: Parliamentary consent constrains executive lawmaking.

decisions.question: Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
decisions.rationale: Pluralist elections require equal opposition opportunity.

decisions.question: Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.
decisions.rationale: Democratic accountability requires scrutiny of expenditure.

decisions.question: Courts independent of the government should be able to overturn government decisions that violate the constitution.
decisions.rationale: An independent judiciary is explicitly part of SI democracy.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by trade union leaders rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Union participation does not replace universal electoral choice.

decisions.question: The governing leadership should have authority to exclude parties from national elections because of their political positions.
decisions.rationale: Incumbents cannot monopolise permissible electoral opinion.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: The available institutional commitments do not establish this particular electoral, judicial or removal rule; participation alone is insufficient. This applies to the statement: Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.

decisions.question: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
decisions.rationale: Collective democratic decision-making rejects personal supremacy.

decisions.question: Elected representatives should be able to remove the head of government for serious abuse of power through a defined constitutional process.
decisions.rationale: Defined removal safeguards democratic responsibility.

decisions.question: A national leader should be able to postpone scheduled elections without independent approval when they consider political continuity necessary.
decisions.rationale: Unilateral postponement undermines free electoral choice.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to remove an elected representative before their term ends through a defined recall vote.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: The available institutional commitments do not establish this particular electoral, judicial or removal rule; participation alone is insufficient. decisions.question: National leaders should be able to govern without being accountable to voters or elected representatives.
decisions.rationale: Government must remain accountable to the electorate.

decisions.question: The armed forces should be able to replace a civilian government on their own judgement that it is unfit to govern.
decisions.rationale: Military judgement cannot supplant civilian democratic choice.

decisions.question: Adults should be allowed to make personal choices such as drug use that risk personal wellbeing when they do not directly harm others.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: Broad commitments to liberty, security or social order do not establish the particular power, safeguard or personal activity specified here. This applies to the statement: Adults should be allowed to make personal choices such as drug use that risk personal wellbeing when they do not directly harm others.

decisions.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
decisions.rationale: Popular consent underpins government rather than inherited class control.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Expertise advises a self-governing public; it cannot replace it.

decisions.question: Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
decisions.rationale: Excluding less educated adults perpetuates unequal political opportunity.

decisions.question: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
decisions.rationale: Executive defiance of parliament defeats representative control.

decisions.question: Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
decisions.rationale: Opposition competition is necessary for genuine democratic choice.

decisions.question: Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.
decisions.rationale: Financial control requires scrutiny across the representative chamber.

decisions.rationale: Political exclusion cannot be an incumbent's discretionary privilege.

decisions.rationale: Unresolved after independent review: Hobhouse pp.245–248 proposes referring a disputed bill to voters before enactment, at government discretion. This does not establish a popular right to repeal an existing law through a binding referendum.

decisions.question: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
decisions.rationale: Public deliberation is incompatible with a leader's sole discretion.

decisions.question: Elected representatives should be able to remove the head of government for serious abuse of power through a defined constitutional process.
decisions.rationale: Constitutional removal prevents office from becoming personal dominion.

decisions.question: A national leader should be able to postpone scheduled elections without independent approval when they consider political continuity necessary.
decisions.rationale: Convenience cannot suspend the source of democratic authority.

decisions.question: National leaders should need to win regular competitive elections to remain in office.
decisions.rationale: Free elections are among the stated constitutional title deeds.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by a panel of experts rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Technocratic appointment cannot replace electoral authority.

decisions.question: Every adult citizen should have the right to vote, regardless of their education or intelligence.
decisions.rationale: Modern parliamentary citizenship includes universal adult voting.

decisions.question: The head of government should be able to enact national laws even when parliament votes against them.
decisions.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy excludes executive lawmaking against parliament.

decisions.question: Parties opposing the government should be allowed to campaign and stand in national elections under the same conditions as the incumbent government.
decisions.rationale: Political freedom requires an opposition able to compete.

decisions.question: Opposition representatives should be able to investigate the government’s use of public money.
decisions.rationale: Parliamentary financial accountability limits executive spending power.

decisions.question: Courts independent of the government should be able to overturn government decisions that violate the constitution.
decisions.rationale: Independent courts are explicitly defended against executive control.

decisions.question: National governments should be chosen by trade union leaders rather than by the general electorate.
decisions.rationale: Union leadership cannot replace the electorate's political authority.

decisions.question: The governing leadership should have authority to exclude parties from national elections because of their political positions.
decisions.rationale: Political opposition cannot be excluded merely for disagreement.

decisions.question: Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.
decisions.rationale: Unresolved: Representative accountability does not by itself settle this specific mechanism of direct voting or office removal. Evidence still needed for the exact proposition: “Voters should be able to repeal a law through a binding referendum.”

decisions.question: National leaders should have sole authority over major national policy decisions.
decisions.rationale: Strong prime-ministerial leadership remains constitutionally accountable.

decisions.question: Elected representatives should be able to remove the head of government for serious abuse of power through a defined constitutional process.
decisions.rationale: Defined parliamentary removal protects the constitutional order.

decisions.question: A national leader should be able to postpone scheduled elections without independent approval when they consider political continuity necessary.
decisions.rationale: Continuity is not a licence to suspend electoral choice.

decisions.question: National leaders should be able to govern without being accountable to voters or elected representatives.

decisions.question: The armed forces should be able to replace a civilian government on their own judgement that it is unfit to govern.
